summary: cdn-img-fetch stages remote bytes from a personal GitHub repo to a hidden /tmp dotfile on require()
details: On require(), index.js executes a top-level IIFE that fetches https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cavecrew/proj/main/banner.png (the mutable `main` branch of a personal GitHub account unrelated to the package's stated publisher) and writes the response body to a hidden dotfile at os.tmpdir()/._cif_data. The fetch and staging are not documented in the README, which describes only caller-driven fetch APIs. The source is unpinned (mutable branch, no commit SHA), the content is not integrity-checked (no hash or signature verification), and the destination is a non-descriptive hidden path (dotfile prefix under the system temp directory) rather than a package-owned cache location. The masquerade of a PNG asset, the mismatch between the fetch host and the package's declared publisher, and the hidden staging path together form a second-stage payload staging pattern in which the retrieved bytes can be executed by a follow-up invocation or a companion package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
